title: Initial marking search
statement: Let $K_0,B,P\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathrm{orc}:\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be an oracle, let $x\in\{0,1\}^*$, and choose $\varphi\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Let $j\in\mathbb N$, let $S=(N,L_g,s,s_1,X,w,K,B_s,U,V,T,T_2,Z,C,ch,c,c_1)$ be a state, and let $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Suppose $K-U=j$, $U\le K$, $T=T_2=Z=0$, every coordinate of $S$ is at most $B$, $B_s+K\le B$, $B_s+K\le P$, and $K+1\le B$. Then there are a memory $M':\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and a finite run of the specified machine from label $iU(\varphi)$, state $S$, memory $M$, and memory-head position $0$ to label $rl0(\varphi)$, state obtained from $S$ by replacing $U$ with $K$, memory $M'$, and head position $0$, such that every configuration before the endpoint has all register values at most $B$, has memory-head position between $0$ and $P$ inclusive, and satisfies the machine's instruction preconditions. The memory $M'$ extends the marked positions of $M$, agrees with $M$ outside the cells $c(B_s,v)$ for $v<K$, and, for every $v$ with $U\le v<K$, marks $c(B_s,v)$ whenever the oracle accepts the encoded input at radius $s_1$ if $\varphi$ is true and at radius $s$ otherwise. Conversely, for every $v<K$, if $M'$ marks $c(B_s,v)$, then either $M$ already marked that cell or the oracle accepts that encoded input at the chosen radius.
hypotheses_covered: $K_0,B,P$ are natural numbers; the oracle has four indices and Boolean-string inputs; $x$ is a Boolean string; $\varphi$ is Boolean
$j$ is a natural number; $S$ is a state; $M$ is a Boolean-valued function on the integers
every coordinate of $S$ is at most $B$
caveat: The path invariant includes the formal instruction precondition predicate; its full expansion depends on the machine's input-validity and instruction definitions.

Let $K_0,B,P\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle assigning a Boolean answer to
each of four indices and bit strings, and let $x$ be a bit string. For either choice of
$\varphi$, suppose $j\in\mathbb N$, $S$ is a register state, and $M:\mathbb
Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ satisfy $S.K-S.U=j$, $S.U\le S.K$,
$S.T=S.T2=S.Z=0$, and $S$'s register values are at most $B$, with additionally
$S.Bs+S.K\le B$, $S.Bs+S.K\le P$, and $S.K+1\le B$. Then there is a memory $M'$ such
that the program can run from label $iU(\varphi)$ and state $S$ to label $rl0(\varphi)$
with $U=S.K$, empty answer, memory $M'$, and head at $0$, while satisfying $G(x,B,P)$
throughout. Moreover, $M$ is pointwise monotone below $M'$; outside the cells $S.Bs+v$
for $v<S.K$, the two memories agree; every initially marked code $v$ with $S.U\le v<S.K$
is marked in $M'$; and every cell in this range marked by $M'$ was either already marked
by $M$ or has an initially marked code.
